title: CRISPR genome editing to first approved edited sickle-cell therapy
sourceNativeSummary: Programmable genome editing moved from laboratory mechanism/platform to an ex-vivo cell-manufacturing, clinical and regulatory system. FDA approval of Casgevy in December 2023 marked the first FDA-approved treatment using this genome-editing technology.
rivalOrBoundary: A transferable editing operation did not itself constitute a therapy; patient-cell collection, ex-vivo editing, conditioning, manufacturing, clinical evidence and regulatory review were required.
